newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CEPA proposes new Java plant terms -- paper.
newsitem.headline: CEPA proposes new Java plant terms -- paper.

text.p: Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) has proposed to the Indonesian government to lower the price of electricity to be generated from its planned Java plant to 6.5-to-6.8 U.S. cents from 7.3 cents, the Sing Tao Daily said on Monday.
CEPA also decided to move the location of the plant to a site 500 meters from the original site agreed on, the newspaper quoted an informed source as saying.
Since the Indonesian government recently revised down the profit tax to 30 perecnt from 35 perecnt so the electricity price needed to be refixed, the source told Sing Tao.
He expected the final terms could be fixed in a month's time and he was confident that the plant could be completed in 1999.
CEPA and Hopewell officials were not immediately available for comment.
Indonesian state electricity firm PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN) said in August it would discuss delays in the project with Hopewell Holdings Ltd, CEPA's parent.
Jakarta had said the project was behind schedule and warned the company its contract could be terminated.
